subject: Hosted API landing copy — privacy/transfer & subprocessor clarifications
messages:
From: Emma Torres <emma.torres@acme-analytics.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick clarifications on your hosted API privacy blurb for our procurement team

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for sending over the draft landing blurb for Redwood's hosted API — our procurement and legal teams asked for a couple of clarifications before we put the vendor in the procurement queue. I attached a short PDF with their questions. High level asks:

- Can you confirm whether customer content is included in any of the listed subprocessors (we need a yes/no plus the list and region).
- How do you describe cross-border data movement on the public landing page without exposing operational detail? They want a two-line explanation they can include in an internal deck.
- Is there a short fallback statement we can use that links to a DPA for deeper terms?

If you can provide suggested copy aimed at a non-technical procurement audience (two or three bullets, plain language) and point to the DPA location, that would be ideal.

Best,
Emma
Procurement, Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme_privacy_questions.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Emma Torres <emma.torres@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on your hosted API privacy blurb for our procurement team

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks and the PDF. Looping in Laura and Kim from Product/Legal ops to draft public-friendly wording and the pointing link to the DPA.

Short answers up front:
- Subprocessors: yes — we use a limited set of cloud providers and telemetry vendors; I attached our subprocessor map (CSV) and will also attach a 1–2 sentence summary for the landing page.
- Cross-border movement: we can provide a two-line plain-language statement that explains data routing and the option to pin residency for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted we’ll describe safeguards and a link to the DPA.
- Link to DPA: we host a downloadable DPA and an executive summary. I will include a short fallback sentence for procurement decks that links to the DPA doc.

We should be careful not to enumerate operational regions on the landing page — instead give a short remit: where data may be processed and a pointer to the subprocessor map.

Action: Laura and Kim — can you draft 2–3 bullet candidates (plain lang) and a one-line fallback link for the procurement slide? ETA Monday EOD?

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, Emma Torres <emma.torres@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 11:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on your hosted API privacy blurb for our procurement team

Thanks — draft below. I kept each option short so procurement can paste it straight into a slide. See comments inline on trade-offs.

Option A — minimal, procurement-friendly (recommended for landing + deck)
• What we process: "We process customer requests and responses to provide the hosted API service. We do not use customer content to train models."
• Where it may be processed: "Data may be processed in geographic regions where our cloud providers operate; we publish an up-to-date subprocessor map."
• Link line (fallback): "See our Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and subprocessor map for full details: [DPA link]."

Trade-offs: clear and short but doesn't state the word 'transfer'; avoids operational region listing.

Option B — slightly more explicit (good for procurement slides)
• What we process: "Customer prompts, generated outputs, and service metadata needed to deliver the API."
• Transfers: "Redwood may route or store data across countries to serve low-latency requests; we use contractual and technical safeguards described in our DPA."
• Link line: "Download our DPA and view subprocessors: [DPA link]."

Trade-offs: better for teams that care about cross-border movement language.

Subprocessor note (for Acme legal):
- The attached CSV is our current subprocessor map. We only list commercial cloud providers (compute/storage), telemetry vendors used for platform health, and our encryption key management partner. We can provide a signed attestation if your procurement needs it.

Attachments I prepared: draft-hosted-privacy-snippet.md (contains the two options above)

Next steps: Kim — can you sanity-check the legal framing (especially the 'we do not use content to train models' line), and confirm the DPA link and attestation process? Emma — tell us if Option A or B fits better for Acme's deck.

Laura Bennett
Product Counsel (Privacy Focus)
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Emma Torres <emma.torres@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on your hosted API privacy blurb for our procurement team

Emma / team — quick legal check and final copy below. I kept the commitments high-level and added the DPA link. We should avoid operational detail on public pages; for procurement we can share an annex under NDA.

Final suggested landing/deck copy (single-paragraph + bullet):
"Redwood processes the content you send to our hosted API to provide inference services. We do not use customer content to improve or train our models unless you explicitly opt in under a separate agreement. Data may be processed in locations where our cloud providers operate; contractual safeguards and encryption are applied for cross-border processing — see our DPA for details."

Three-line bullet for procurement slide:
• What: "Processes customer requests and service metadata; no training on customer content without opt-in."
• Where: "May be processed across provider regions; see subprocessor map for specifics."
• Link: "DPA & subprocessors: https://redwood.ai/dpa (attestation available under request)."

Attachments: draft-hosted-privacy-snippet.md (finalized), subprocessor-map.csv (latest).

Emma — if that reads OK, I'll share a redlined DPA link and a short attestation template. If Acme requires region-by-region residency guarantees, we can route them to Dedicated/Private offerings.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
